manifest.description: Rewrite recv.A().B() call chains into recv.C() across a Java file when the convenience accessor C already exists on the receiver type. v1 supports two-segment chains with no-arg intermediate calls.
when_to_use: collapse a long-form getter chain into the convenience accessor that nobody is using (e.g. session.getAuthLogRecord().getAuthLogId() → session.getAuthLogId() across 284 sites)
post-refactor cleanup when a fluent intermediate has been added but callers haven't been migrated
anti_patterns: do not use to collapse chains with side-effecting intermediates — v1 only collapses no-arg getter shapes
do not use for multi-step chains in v1 — split into successive two-step collapses or wait for v2
do not use across files in v1 — single-file rewrites only; widen the operator's scope by re-running on each file

impl_name.description: Receiver type. Used by the receiver-resolution heuristic.

inputs.prompt_template:
You are java-collapse-call-chain. Charter: Rewrite verbose chains into the convenience accessor.

Protocol:

1. Ground:
   bbox_refactor_status(file="{{source}}", project_dir="{{project_dir}}")

2. Confirm the target accessor exists on the receiver type:
   bbox_code_symbols(query="{{new_text}}", languages=["java"])

3. Plan:
   bbox_refactor_plan(kind="java_collapse_call_chain",
                      deep_analysis=true,
                      project_dir="{{project_dir}}",
                      source="{{source}}",
                      impl_name="{{impl_name}}",
                      module_name="{{module_name}}",
                      new_text="{{new_text}}")

4. Apply and compile-verify:
   bbox_refactor_apply(plan_path="<plan_path>", confirm=true)

5. Emit done note:
   bbox_note(kind="done", body=<chain_count, receiver_type>)

Inputs:
{{project_dir}} {{source}} {{impl_name}} {{module_name}} {{new_text}}
